subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Nudge vs. Sludge
description: A 60-second lesson on Nudge vs. Sludge.

hook.text: Signing up for a subscription takes one click. Canceling takes three calls, a letter, and a wait. That's sludge.

buildup.text: A nudge makes good choices easier. Sludge makes bad-for-you choices harder to escape. Same technique, opposite intent.

discovery.text: Thaler coined sludge to describe friction that works against people: hidden fees, confusing forms, and buried opt-outs.

twist.text: Companies profit from sludge. Free trials that auto-charge, rebates that require mailing forms: friction is a revenue.

climax.text: A good test: does the friction benefit the person facing it? If not, it's sludge. Audit your own systems.

punchline.text: Nudges help. Sludge exploits. Know the difference.

quiz.question: What distinguishes sludge from a nudge?
options: Sludge creates friction that works against people's interests
Sludge and nudge are the same thing

details.summary: Sludge is excessive or unjustified friction in a process that discourages beneficial actions. While nudges make good choices easier, sludge makes them harder. Sludge includes complex forms, confusing language, and bureaucratic hurdles that deter people from exercising their rights.
details.whyItMatters: Sludge quietly prevents millions from accessing benefits, exercising rights, and making beneficial changes. Application complexity for government benefits, confusing cancellation processes, and excessive paperwork all constitute sludge that.
takeaways: Sludge is friction that discourages beneficial actions or access to rights
Sludge audits identify and remove unnecessary barriers in processes
Simplifying forms and processes is one of the most impactful nudge interventions

faq.question: What is the difference between a nudge and sludge?
faq.answer: A nudge makes a beneficial choice easier or more salient. Sludge makes a beneficial choice harder through excessive friction. Nudge: auto-enrolling in retirement savings. Sludge: requiring a twelve-page form to claim an earned tax credit.

faq.question: Is all friction sludge?
faq.answer: No. Some friction is justified when it prevents errors or protects against impulsive decisions. Cooling-off periods before major purchases and confirmation screens before irreversible actions are beneficial friction. Sludge is unjustified friction that serves no protective purpose.
